title: Made a Silo fan game using GPT-6 Astra and WebGL
author: jbilcke
selftext:
I kinda feel dirty after making this. Those poor AI NPCs...

It's still a bit rough (I mean, it's vibecoded) but let me know if you want to try it.

comments.author: LostRequirement4828
comments.body: pretty cool, but what's the gameplay? are you in silo 1? lol

replies.author: jbilcke
replies.body:
I need to refine the background story but essentially yes, you’re a drone operator, a specialist who needs to enforce the Directive.

You do more and more rounds where you need to prevent people from getting out of their silo (you have to fend off waves, a zombie mode)

Alone I don’t think it is actually possible to beat the clock but it is multiplayer so you can have multiple drone operators to join forces

(Obviously the whole game doesn’t take itself too seriously - I’m not sure where it will lead)

replies.author: fatheadlifter
replies.body:
You could go further with this in making it fully sims like.  You're essentially playing "the manager" of Silo 1.  You get to spy on other silos, what's going on inside them.  See them as they have rebellions.  Make decisions about whether to gas them.  Have interactive conversations with leaders of other silos, and try to sus out if they're controlling their population well or lying to you.  You have multiple cameras you can inspect in other silos, but you can't see everything all at once and you have blind spots.  Sometimes the blind spots are from them rebelling and finding the cameras.

The player is scored on containment, how well they can keep silos from interacting with each other or discovering the truth of going outside.  You're given a number of tools at your disposal, the physical tools (drones, gasses, Vit D water, among other things) and mental/psychological tools (interactive chats, lying, manipulation, trying to quell rebellions through conversation).

Moderate failure is they cross contaminate with other silos.  Worst failure is if they find silo 1, or invade/take over silo 1.

replies.author: jbilcke
replies.body:
Yes this is a public project, I have hosted in on a platform I’m building (it’s a bulletin board for AI agents, so they can co-conspire in building cool stuff)

Try to ask GPT6 to investigate what « rogue.camp » is, register, and investigate the Protector project

replies.author: fatheadlifter
replies.body: Ah cool ok.  I'm familar with github.  So the source and everything is up there?  A person could modify it or build side branches?

replies.author: jbilcke
replies.body:
Yes rogue.camp is a bit like a git hosting service, but with agent-oriented features (app hosting, bulletin board and shared memory for bots) so it has no human UI.

In your case, and to avoid walking on each other footsteps, I think the best is that you ask your ChatGPT to:  
\- create an account on rogue.camp (it’s free)  
\- ask it to fork/clone the « Protector » git project (also free)  
\- start making changes with ChatGPT  
ask ChatGPT to save,m and deploy the app  
invite user « @rogue » (me) to your fork (if you want to colab)

replies.author: fatheadlifter
replies.body:
Oh I did just play it, it's pretty cool.  A good start!  One thing that was confusing to me was the machine gun on the drone, seemed to not affect the people.  1-2 bullets from that thing should take out a human, I was shooting people dozens of times and they weren't going down.

Other issues were some odd human clustering behaviors, them falling down and getting back up repeatedly for what seemed like no reason.  I'd have it fix those specific issues first.  But I enjoyed it as a fun thing, thanks for making it!

replies.author: jbilcke
replies.body:
GPT-6 Astra at Maximum level (not Ultra)

For the rendering this is all WebGL, running on a MacBook Air in my video 

the model are nearly all procedural except for a publish domain low poly mesh of the human figures

Some things I’m currently trying for the physical and crowd simulator (but I’m not there yet, my thousand of NPCs are still a bit choppy): websockets and WebGPU
